# Data Audit Report — Austin Animal Center Intakes & Outcomes

**Status:** Stage 1 audit complete; awaiting candidate review (DECISION_LOG Stage 2).
**Audit date:** 23-11-2026 · **Generated by:** `python analysis/run_all.py`
**Sources (unchanged, SHA-256 in `data/reference/source_checksums.csv`):**
`data/raw/Austin_Animal_Center_Intakes__10_01_2013_to_05_05_2025_.csv`,
`data/raw/Austin_Animal_Center_Outcomes__10_01_2013_to_05_05_2025_.csv`

Every number in this report is produced by the scripts and can be found in the CSV named next to it.
Dates are shown as DD-MM-YYYY; stored data keeps genuine date/datetime types.

## 1. Summary

| | Intakes | Outcomes | Source |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Rows | 173,812 | 173,775 | `outputs/audit/source_file_profile.csv` |
| Columns | 12 | 12 | |
| Exact duplicate excess rows | 36 | 26 | |
| Rows after exact-duplicate removal (analytic events) | 173,776 | 173,749 | |
| Unique Animal IDs | 156,287 | 156,237 | |
| Animal IDs with 2+ rows | 13,487 | 13,507 | |
| Excess rows from repeated IDs (rows − unique IDs) | 17,525 | 17,538 | |
| Rows belonging to repeated IDs | 31,012 | 31,045 | |
| Same ID + timestamp, other fields differ | 12 rows (6 pairs) | 2 rows (1 pair) | `same_id_timestamp_conflicts.csv` |
| First / last timestamp | 01-10-2013 07:51 / 04-05-2025 23:44 | 01-10-2013 09:31 / 05-05-2025 07:22 | `date_quality.csv` |

**Overall assessment.** The files are structurally clean: every timestamp parses, every Animal ID has
the form `A` + 6 digits, `MonthYear` agrees with the timestamp on 100% of rows, and core
categorical fields (intake type, animal type, outcome type) are complete apart from 46 blank outcome
types. The material issues are (i) Animal ID is not a visit key, (ii) 3,788 outcome timestamps are
date-only (midnight), (iii) outcome subtype is 54.16% blank, (iv) category definitions change over time,
and (v) small numbers of duplicates, negative ages and DOB-after-outcome rows. None justifies deleting
records; all are flagged in the derived data. Detail: `docs/DATA_QUALITY_ISSUES.md`.

All preliminary inventory figures in DECISION_LOG §5 reproduce exactly. One definitional correction:
the "17,525 / 17,538 rows belonging to repeated IDs" are *excess* rows (rows − unique IDs); the
number of rows that belong to a repeated ID is 31,012 / 31,045.

## 3. Duplicates and repeated identifiers

Three different things are distinguished (`outputs/audit/duplicate_summary.csv`):

1. **Exact duplicate rows** — every column identical. 36 intake and 26 outcome excess copies, each
   in a pair (36 and 26 groups). Flagged `is_exact_duplicate`; the first copy is kept as the analytic
   event, the excess copy is retained in the cleaned file but excluded from matching and counts.
   Lists: `exact_duplicate_rows_intakes.csv`, `exact_duplicate_rows_outcomes.csv`.
2. **Suspected duplicate events** — same Animal ID and timestamp but differing in another field
   (6 intake pairs, mostly Found Location and/or Intake Type; 1 outcome pair differing in subtype), plus
   consecutive same-kind events less than 24 hours apart with no opposite event between them
   (10 intake and 17 outcome instances; `suspected_duplicate_events.csv`). Retained and flagged;
   the matching rule resolves them and they appear in the ambiguity list where assignment is affected.
3. **Legitimate repeat visits** — 17,489 analytic intake events are a second or later intake for the
   same Animal ID. One animal has 33 intakes and 33 outcomes (`animal_id_frequency.csv`).

Cross-file: 155,423 Animal IDs appear in both files; 864 only in intakes (mostly 2024–2025 intakes
still open at extract end); 814 only in outcomes (704 of their 814 analytic outcome rows are dated 2013, consistent
with intakes before the 01-10-2013 extract start). No Animal ID has more than one animal type across the
two files (`cross_dataset_consistency.csv`).

## 4. Dates, times and timezone

* **Intakes** — `MM/DD/YYYY hh:mm:ss AM/PM`, month-first, no offset, 100% parse. Only 58 at midnight.
* **Outcomes** — ISO-8601. 170,191 rows have no offset; 3,584 rows end in `-05:00`. **All 3,584
  offset rows are exactly `00:00:00`**, and 884 of them fall in November–February, when Austin's
  true offset is `-06:00`. The offset is therefore an export artefact on date-only records, not a
  timezone. A further 204 non-offset outcomes are also exactly midnight (3,788 midnight in total).
* **Interpretation (D-008):** both files are read as source-local wall-clock time, timezone-naive.
  No conversion is applied (converting the offset rows to UTC would move them to 05:00 and is not
  supported by the evidence). The offset is kept in `outcome_tz_offset`; date-only rows are flagged.
* **MonthYear** agrees with the parsed timestamp on every row of both files, confirming wall-clock
  interpretation (preliminary §6.4 note retested and confirmed).
* **Coverage / partial years:** intakes 01-10-2013 to 04-05-2025; outcomes 01-10-2013 to 05-05-2025.
  2013 (Oct–Dec) and 2025 (Jan–early May) are partial. The last full day present in both files is
  04-05-2025; like-for-like windows use 01-01 to 04-05 and 01-10 to 31-12 (D-015).
* No timestamp is later than the extract end; no parse failures. Outcome seconds are non-zero on
  4,772 rows (intake seconds are always zero) — a precision difference between systems, not an error.

## 5. Ages and dates of birth

`outputs/audit/age_and_dob_exceptions.csv`

* Age text is `N day(s)/week(s)/month(s)/year(s)`; converted to approximate days (year = 365.25,
  month = 30.4375). Parse success > 99.99%.
* 10 negative ages in each file (`-1 years` ×6, `-2` ×1, `-3` ×2, `-4` ×1); 9 outcome ages are
  `NULL`. Flagged `age_upon_*_invalid`; assigned age band "Invalid / unknown".
* 33 outcome rows have a date of birth after the outcome date (flag `dob_after_outcome`).
* For 100% of matched visits, the intake age differs from the age implied by the outcome-file DOB
  by less than one year (median 1.25 days), i.e. within the rounding of the age text. This indicates
  the source *derives* age from DOB; age therefore cannot independently validate stay length.

Animal type (intake rows): Dog 94,608 (54.43%), Cat 69,324 (39.88%), Other 8,968, Bird 878,
Livestock 34. Intake condition: Normal 147,141 (84.66%), Injured 10,805, Sick 7,939, Nursing 3,878,
Neonatal 1,971, and 15 smaller labels.

**Labels and spelling.** No leading/trailing whitespace in any field. Case/punctuation variants:
only `Blue Cream` vs `Blue/Cream` in Color (`label_variants.csv`). Semantically overlapping labels
are listed for review, not merged (`semantic_label_review.csv`, D-014): Medical / Med Attn /
Med Urgent; Neonatal / Nursing as "conditions"; Emergency / Emer; Foster / In Foster; Snr / SCRP;
Rto-Adopt vs Return to Owner; Missing / Lost / Stolen.

**Definitions change over time** (`outputs/analysis/annual_intakes_by_type.csv`): the intake type
*Abandoned* first appears in 2020; *Euthanasia Request* falls from 110 rows (2014) to ≤ 4 per year
from 2018. Category trends across 2020 therefore partly reflect coding changes.

## 7. Visit matching (summary)

Full method: `docs/VISIT_MATCHING_METHODOLOGY.md`.

* No sequence field exists in either file. The earlier "Animal ID + sequence" was a derived rank.
* Recommended rule `adjacent_dp`: 172,772 matched visits; 1,004 unmatched intakes; 977 unmatched
  outcomes; 0 reused intakes; 0 negative durations; 0 overlapping visits; 0 animal-type mismatches.
* LOS (days): P25 2.00, P50 6.00, P75 19.89, P90 55.34, P95 84.72, P99 214.24; 577 visits > 365 days.

## 8. Time-series validation (summary)

`outputs/analysis/annual_event_counts.csv`, `like_for_like_periods.csv`, `seasonality_index.csv`,
`structural_break_screen.csv`

* Annual raw-row counts reproduce preliminary §6.6 exactly for every year (analytic-event counts
  differ by the exact duplicates only).
* **2020 vs 2019:** intake events −51.41%, outcome events −50.56%. Monthly year-over-year change is
  −2.0% in 01-2020 and +1.2% in 02-2020, then −41.2% (03-2020) and −80.8% (04-2020). The structural
  break screen places the largest 12-month level shift at 03-2020 (−58.5%). The data establish the
  timing, not the cause.
* **Level shift persists:** full-year intake events averaged 18,216 (2014–2019) and 11,643
  (2022–2024), about 36% lower. The like-for-like window 01-01 to 04-05 gives 3,745 intakes in
  2025 vs 3,991 in 2024 (−6.2%).
* **Seasonality** (full years 2014–2024): intake index peaks in May (127.4) and June (121.9) and
  troughs in February (77.7) and December (80.4); outcomes peak in July (119.6).

## 9. Implications for the Power BI model

1. Use `outputs/matching/candidate_visits.csv` as the visit fact table (filter
   `visit_status = "Matched visit"` for LOS and outcome rates); keep intake and outcome event tables
   for event-count trends. Relate on `intake_event_id` / `outcome_event_id`, not Animal ID.
2. Implement LOS as a measure over `los_days`; expose `same_day_visit`, `match_rule` and
   `outcome_status_provisional` as filters for sensitivity checks.
3. Mark 2013 and 2025 as partial years in the date table; build year-over-year measures on full years
   or like-for-like windows only.
4. Do not report the provisional live-outcome share as the City live-release rate (open question §12 Q4);
   wildlife ("Other" with intake type Wildlife) is 87.1% euthanasia and must be handled per the
   official definition once verified.
